title: Text Processing Validation and Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of text processing validation and testing and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply testing string functions in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Text Processing Validation and Testing is part of Strings, Regular Expressions, and Text Processing. Start with testing string functions and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Text processing should distinguish matching values from near-misses and account for missing text and encoding.

content_blocks.title: Visual guide: Text Processing Validation and Testing
content_blocks.alt_text: Concept visual supporting lesson 92, Text Processing Validation and Testing. The module and lesson flow is shown with labelled steps and verification checkpoints.
content_blocks.caption: Use the visual to orient the topic, then validate the details in the example and official references.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Text processing should distinguish matching values from near-misses and account for missing text and encoding. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Testing String Functions
items.text: Turn testing string functions into a check with a clear condition, expected result and an example that should fail.

items.title: Testing Edge Cases
items.text: Turn testing edge cases into a check with a clear condition, expected result and an example that should fail.

items.title: Handling Missing Text
items.text: For handling missing text, include a failing or boundary case and explain how it should be detected without silently losing information.

items.title: Regex Performance and Readability
items.text: Explain regex performance and readability in the context of text processing validation and testing, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Building a Text-Cleaning Utility
items.text: Build the smallest example for building a text-cleaning utility, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Test at least one matching string, one non-match and one boundary or non-ASCII value. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Text Processing Validation and Testing
content_blocks.code:

content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Check matching and non-matching text, whitespace, missing strings and encoding assumptions. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For text processing validation and testing, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply text processing validation and testing to a small synthetic example. Start with testing string functions, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.

Inspect the type and shape of the result, then test one ordinary and one boundary input.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
